competencies.name: Arithmetic
competencies.description: Fundamental operations with numbers including addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division

competencies.name: Pre-Algebra
competencies.description: Foundation for algebra including integers, fractions, decimals, and basic equations

prerequisites.notes: Arithmetic fundamentals are essential for understanding pre-algebra concepts

competencies.name: Algebra I
competencies.description: Study of linear equations, inequalities, polynomials, and factoring

prerequisites.notes: Pre-algebra concepts are foundational for Algebra I

competencies.name: Algebra II
competencies.description: Advanced algebraic concepts including quadratic equations, exponential functions, and logarithms

prerequisites.notes: Algebra I is essential foundation for Algebra II concepts

competencies.name: Geometry
competencies.description: Study of shapes, sizes, positions, and properties of space including points, lines, angles, and solids

prerequisites.notes: Basic algebra helps with geometric proofs and calculations

competencies.name: Trigonometry
competencies.description: Study of relationships between angles and sides of triangles, including sine, cosine, and tangent functions

prerequisites.notes: Algebra II provides necessary foundation for understanding trigonometric concepts
Geometric understanding is essential for trigonometry

competencies.name: Pre-Calculus
competencies.description: Advanced preparation for calculus including functions, analytical geometry, and trigonometry

prerequisites.notes: Algebra II is essential for pre-calculus
Trigonometry is a major component of pre-calculus

competencies.name: Calculus I
competencies.description: Introduction to differential calculus including limits, derivatives, and their applications

prerequisites.notes: Pre-calculus provides essential foundation for understanding limits and derivatives

competencies.name: Calculus II
competencies.description: Integral calculus including techniques of integration, applications, and series

prerequisites.notes: Calculus I is essential foundation for integral calculus

competencies.name: Calculus III
competencies.description: Multivariable calculus including partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus

prerequisites.notes: Calculus II concepts extend naturally to multiple variables

competencies.name: Linear Algebra
competencies.description: Study of vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, and systems of linear equations

prerequisites.notes: Strong algebraic foundation is essential for linear algebra
Calculus helps with understanding some linear algebra applications

competencies.name: Differential Equations
competencies.description: Study of equations involving derivatives and their solutions, with applications in science and engineering

prerequisites.notes: Integration techniques from Calculus II are essential for solving differential equations
Linear algebra is useful for systems of differential equations

competencies.name: Partial Differential Equations
competencies.description: Study of differential equations with multiple independent variables

prerequisites.notes: Multivariable calculus is essential for PDEs
Understanding ODEs is foundational for PDEs

competencies.name: Real Analysis
competencies.description: Rigorous study of real numbers, sequences, series, continuity, and differentiability

prerequisites.notes: Calculus provides intuition that real analysis makes rigorous

competencies.name: Complex Analysis
competencies.description: Study of functions of complex variables including analytic functions and contour integration

prerequisites.notes: Single variable calculus extends to complex variables

competencies.name: Abstract Algebra
competencies.description: Study of algebraic structures including groups, rings, and fields

prerequisites.notes: Linear algebra provides concrete examples of algebraic structures

competencies.name: Statistics
competencies.description: Collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation of data

prerequisites.notes: Algebraic skills are needed for statistical formulas and calculations

competencies.name: Probability
competencies.description: Mathematical study of randomness, chance events, and their likelihood

prerequisites.notes: Algebra is essential for probability calculations

competencies.name: Bayesian Statistics
competencies.description: Statistical inference using Bayes' theorem and prior probability distributions

prerequisites.notes: Foundation in statistics is essential for Bayesian methods
Probability theory is core to Bayesian statistics

competencies.name: Discrete Mathematics
competencies.description: Study of mathematical structures that are discrete rather than continuous, including logic, sets, and graph theory

prerequisites.notes: Basic algebra is needed for discrete math concepts

competencies.name: Graph Theory
competencies.description: Study of graphs as mathematical structures modeling relationships between objects

prerequisites.notes: Discrete math provides helpful background for graph theory

competencies.name: Combinatorics
competencies.description: Study of counting, arrangement, and combination of objects

prerequisites.notes: Algebra is essential for combinatorial formulas

competencies.name: Number Theory
competencies.description: Study of properties and relationships of integers, including prime numbers and divisibility

prerequisites.notes: Algebraic reasoning is essential for number theory

competencies.name: Mathematical Logic
competencies.description: Study of formal systems, proof theory, and the foundations of mathematics

prerequisites.notes: Discrete math introduces logical reasoning concepts

competencies.name: Set Theory
competencies.description: Study of collections of objects and their properties, fundamental to modern mathematics

prerequisites.notes: Discrete math introduces basic set concepts

competencies.name: Topology
competencies.description: Study of properties preserved under continuous deformations including space, dimension, and continuity

prerequisites.notes: Real analysis provides foundation for topological concepts

competencies.name: Numerical Analysis
competencies.description: Study of algorithms for solving mathematical problems numerically

prerequisites.notes: Calculus is essential for understanding numerical methods
Linear algebra is used extensively in numerical algorithms

competencies.name: Operations Research
competencies.description: Application of mathematical methods to optimize decision-making in complex systems

prerequisites.notes: Linear programming and optimization require linear algebra
Statistical methods are used in OR

competencies.name: Game Theory
competencies.description: Mathematical study of strategic decision-making and competitive interactions

prerequisites.notes: Probability is essential for analyzing game strategies
Linear algebra helps with matrix games

competencies.name: Cryptography
competencies.description: Mathematical foundations of encryption, code-making, and information security

prerequisites.notes: Number theory is fundamental to modern cryptography
Abstract algebra provides tools for advanced cryptography

competencies.name: Optimization
competencies.description: Mathematical techniques for finding best solutions from a set of alternatives

prerequisites.notes: Multivariable calculus is essential for optimization
Linear algebra is fundamental to optimization methods

competencies.name: Mathematical Modeling
competencies.description: Creating mathematical representations of real-world systems and phenomena

prerequisites.notes: Calculus is essential for continuous models
Differential equations model dynamic systems

competencies.name: Actuarial Mathematics
competencies.description: Mathematical and statistical methods for assessing risk in insurance and finance

prerequisites.notes: Probability is fundamental to risk assessment
Statistical methods are core to actuarial work
Calculus is needed for actuarial models

competencies.name: Euclidean Geometry
competencies.description: Classical geometry based on Euclid's axioms studying flat space and geometric figures

prerequisites.notes: Basic geometry provides foundation for Euclidean geometry

competencies.name: Non-Euclidean Geometry
competencies.description: Geometry that rejects Euclid's parallel postulate, including hyperbolic and elliptic geometry

prerequisites.notes: Understanding Euclidean geometry is essential before studying alternatives

competencies.name: Analytic Geometry
competencies.description: Study of geometry using coordinate systems and algebraic principles

prerequisites.notes: Algebra is essential for coordinate-based geometry
Basic geometry concepts are foundational

competencies.name: Differential Geometry
competencies.description: Study of geometric properties using calculus and differential equations

prerequisites.notes: Multivariable calculus is essential for differential geometry
Linear algebra is fundamental to differential geometry

competencies.name: Projective Geometry
competencies.description: Study of geometric properties invariant under projective transformations

prerequisites.notes: Linear algebra provides tools for projective transformations

competencies.name: Measure Theory
competencies.description: Systematic way to assign numbers to sets, foundational for modern probability and analysis

prerequisites.notes: Real analysis is essential foundation for measure theory

competencies.name: Functional Analysis
competencies.description: Study of vector spaces with topological structure and linear operators between them

prerequisites.notes: Real analysis provides foundation for functional spaces
Linear algebra extends to infinite-dimensional spaces in functional analysis

competencies.name: Algebraic Geometry
competencies.description: Study of geometric objects defined by polynomial equations

prerequisites.notes: Abstract algebra is essential for algebraic geometry
Linear algebra provides tools for algebraic geometry

competencies.name: Dynamical Systems
competencies.description: Study of systems that evolve over time according to fixed rules

prerequisites.notes: Differential equations model dynamical systems
Linear algebra is used to analyze system behavior

competencies.name: Stochastic Processes
competencies.description: Mathematical models of random processes evolving over time

prerequisites.notes: Probability theory is fundamental to stochastic processes
Calculus is needed for continuous-time processes

competencies.name: Time Series Analysis
competencies.description: Statistical methods for analyzing data points collected over time

prerequisites.notes: Statistical foundation is essential for time series
Probability helps with forecasting and modeling

competencies.name: Mathematical Statistics
competencies.description: Theoretical foundation of statistical methods using probability and analysis

prerequisites.notes: Probability theory is the foundation of mathematical statistics
Calculus is essential for continuous distributions

competencies.name: Fourier Analysis
competencies.description: Study of representing functions as sums of sinusoidal waves

prerequisites.notes: Integration is essential for Fourier transforms
Fourier analysis is used to solve differential equations

competencies.name: Boolean Algebra
competencies.description: Algebraic structure for logical operations used in digital logic and computer science

prerequisites.notes: Discrete math introduces logical structures

competencies.name: Category Theory
competencies.description: Abstract study of mathematical structures and relationships between them

prerequisites.notes: Abstract algebra provides concrete examples for category theory

competencies.name: Finite Mathematics
competencies.description: Mathematics of finite sets including linear programming, probability, and matrices

prerequisites.notes: Algebra provides foundation for finite mathematics
